title: SMOKE: M156 residual-growth plumbing on tiny cells
_smoke_note: Reduced cells (40000 train / 20000 test rows — the registered probe-derived row count; budget {256} only, anchors and control skipped, floor violations tolerated, GPU path not exercised). Results are INADMISSIBLE as evidence.
question: Does the M156 pipeline (base-head reproduction, error rows, column-extracted arm codes, head fit, append, re-fuse, gate) run end-to-end on tiny cells?

base.note: the promoted SPM+sqrt head (C4 p=0.5, penalty 0.1)

growth.dictionary_note: first g atoms of the cached f6144 pool; arms read the cached memmap columns

control.mechanism: M108 arm (c) blind greedy (group-OMP), SKIPPED in smoke (identity prefix used as the placeholder order)

gate.registered: per budget g: growth_fused >= static + 0.005 AND growth_fused > control_fused (static = the base head's test read)
gate.consequence_passed: residual-targeted growth lifts the global-head system beyond the base read beyond the blind-greedy control.
gate.consequence_fired: M156 closes as a scoped negative on this corpus and the base head stands.

ops_ledger.note: both arms report the g-atom encode-equivalent MACs over train+test rows; the control additionally its error-row pool encode + OMP selection MACs.
